lesson_title: Finance Essentials: The Hole, the Shovel and the Count
hook_text: A vetkoek stall loses money on its first 124 sales of the month. Sale 125 changes everything.
clip_script: The stand costs R1 500 whether he fries or sleeps. That is the hole the month starts in. Each vetkoek sells for R26 but eats R14 of ingredients — so each sale throws R12 into the hole. The only question that matters in week one: how many R12 shovelfuls fill a R1 500 hole? 1 500 over 12 — 125. Vetkoek number 125 lands exactly at ground level: income R3 250, costs R3 250, nothing lost, nothing gained. Vetkoek 126 is the first one he actually profits from — R12 clean. Every break-even question is these three numbers in costume: the hole, the shovel, the count. Gyms, tuck shops, taxi routes — same three numbers, every time.
visual_style: A literal hole labelled R1 500 filling with golden R12 coins one vetkoek at a time, a counter racing to 125, then the ground level breaking into green profit territory at 126.
pacing: Slow reveal of the hole, accelerating coin montage, sharp freeze on sale 125, triumphant beat at 126.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson to master every money move before the final paper.
